mainTopic: Why a כהן may not marry an אילונית or a קטנה, and how many children fulfill פריה ורביה
overview: The גמרא explains that the משנה says 'a כהן' only because רבי יהודה calls an אילונית a זונה, and רב הונא gives the פסוק behind that view. A ברייתא then brings רבי אליעזר's ruling that a כהן may not marry a קטנה. רבה explains that רבי אליעזר combines רבי מאיר's worry about the minority with רבי יהודה's view, but the גמרא challenges both halves from other ברייתות. רב אדא בר אהבה says the ruling is about a כהן גדול, and רבא rejects this. רבא instead explains that any כהן is affected, because a young wife might be seduced, which for a minor counts as אונס. רב פפא and רב נחמן בר יצחק each tie the ruling to a ברייתא teaching that a כהן גדול must marry a נערה. רב עמרם rules against רבי אלעזר's strict view of who is a זונה. A new משנה then teaches how many children fulfill פריה ורביה, and the גמרא discusses whether a man with children must still have a wife and why בית שמאי learn from משה; that answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the משנה says 'a כהן'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. The first part of the משנה says 'a כהן' only because the end of the משנה brings רבי יהודה, who calls an אילונית a זונה, and the זונה prohibition applies only to כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי יהודה says: Even if he has a wife] and has children, he may not marry an אילונית, because she is the זונה that the תורה speaks about. Only כהנים are commanded about a זונה, and ordinary Jews are not. That is why the משנה says 'a כהן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to why the משנה says 'a כהן' when the rule about an אילונית seems to apply to every Jew. It points to רבי יהודה's view at the end of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a man without children should not marry an אילונית applies to every Jewish man, because of the מצוה of having children. But the end of the משנה adds רבי יהודה's reason, that she counts as a זונה, and that reason only matters for כהנים. So the תנא used the word 'כהן' in the first part to match the end of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who never develops physically and cannot have children
A woman forbidden to a כהן under the תורה's rules
They are commanded
It teaches (the משנה says)

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'כהן' in the first part of the משנה does not mean an ordinary Jew may marry an אילונית when he has no children. The rule applies to everyone. The משנה says 'כהן' only because of how its last part is worded.

phrases.english: and he has children —
phrases.notes: We are coming in partway through the quote of רבי יהודה at the end of the משנה: 'even if he has a wife and children.'

phrases.english: he may not marry a woman who cannot bear children,
for she is the zonah stated in the Torah.
And it is priests who were commanded about a zonah,
but ordinary Israelites were not commanded;
because of that, it teaches 'a priest.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי קָתָנֵי כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to the question asked just before this section: why does the משנה say 'כהן' and not every Jew?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording: the first clause is worded to match the last clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying 'כהן' would suggest that only a כהן is forbidden to marry an אילונית when he has no children
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies to everyone. 'כהן' is used only because of רבי יהודה's זונה reason in the last clause, which applies only to כהנים

steps.title: The פסוק behind רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא brings a פסוק in הושע to show why רבי יהודה treats relations with an אילונית as זנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: What is רבי יהודה's reason? The פסוק says: 'They will eat and not be satisfied; they will act like harlots and will not increase.' Any relations that cannot lead to increase are nothing but harlotry.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the source for רבי יהודה's view that an אילונית counts as a זונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links 'harlotry' with 'not increasing.' רב הונא reads this as a rule: relations that can never produce children are treated as זנות. Since an אילונית can never have children, she fits the category of זונה for a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
They will increase or spread out (have children)
Increase; the chance to have children
Relations counted as harlotry

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?
As it is written: 'They will eat and not be satisfied,
they will act like harlots and not increase.'
Any relations that have no chance of increase —
are nothing but relations of harlotry.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the רבי יהודה view mentioned in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations that can never lead to children are treated as זנות, so an אילונית counts as a זונה

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: a כהן may not marry a minor girl
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי אליעזר's ruling that a כהן may not marry a קטנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says: A כהן may not marry a קטנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a surprising ruling about a כהן marrying a young girl. It does not give the reason yet, and the next steps will search for one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the text so far explains why a קטנה would be forbidden to a כהן. That gap is what the following steps try to fill.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A girl under the age of maturity

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
A priest may not marry a minor girl.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related topic: another ruling that connects to רבי יהודה's view that an אילונית is a זונה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן may not marry a קטנה

steps.title: רב חסדא sends רבה to work out the reason
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells רבה to look into רבי אליעזר's ruling, because רב הונא will ask him about it that evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to רבה: Go and look into this, because tonight רב הונא will ask you about it.
steps.whatsHappening: This story sets up the question: what is רבי אליעזר's reason? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is put as a task from רב חסדא to רבה. It shows that the reason was not obvious and needed careful thought.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out and look into it
In the evening
Asks

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said to Rabba:
Go and look into it,

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְאוּרְתָּא בָּעֵי לַהּ רַב הוּנָא מִינָּךְ.
phrases.english: because in the evening Rav Huna will ask it of you.

steps.triggerLanguage: פּוֹק עַיֵּין בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up the search for the reason behind רבי אליעזר's ruling in step 3
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רבי אליעזר forbid a כהן to marry a קטנה?

steps.title: רבה's answer: רבי אליעזר holds like רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבה looked into it and concluded that רבי אליעזר's ruling combines two views: רבי מאיר's and רבי יהודה's.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and looked into it: רבי אליעזר holds like רבי מאיר, and he also holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a short answer. רבי אליעזר's ruling comes from putting two earlier opinions together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither view alone forbids a קטנה. The ruling only works when the two views are combined. The next step explains how each one contributes.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like (agrees with) the opinion of
He went out

phrases.english: He went out and looked into it:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds like Rabbi Meir,
and he holds like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְפַק עַיֵּין בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר's ruling comes from combining the views of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה

steps.title: How the two views combine
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר worries about the minority, so a young girl might turn out to be an אילונית. רבי יהודה holds that an אילונית is a זונה. Together, a כהן may not marry a קטנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority. And he holds like רבי יהודה, who said an אילונית is a זונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains how each opinion adds one piece to רבי אליעזר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a grown woman we can already tell whether she is an אילונית. With a קטנה we cannot tell yet. Most girls are not אילונית, but רבי מאיר does not rely on the majority, so we must consider that she might be one. Since רבי יהודה says an אילונית is a זונה, a כהן must not take the chance.

keyTerms.meaning: He worries about the minority (he does not rely on the majority)
She is (she counts as)

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's explanation: רבי אליעזר's ban = רבי מאיר (worry about the minority: she may turn out to be an אילונית) + רבי יהודה (an אילונית is a זונה). The next steps challenge both halves, and the גמרא ends up looking for a different reason.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a clear example of how the גמרא builds a ruling by putting together two separate principles from different תנאים.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Meir,
who is concerned about the minority.
phrases.notes: Most girls grow up normally, but we still worry this one might turn out to be an אילונית.

phrases.english: And he holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: A woman who cannot bear children is a zonah.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, דְּחָיֵישׁ לְמִיעוּטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the short answer given in step 5
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A כהן may not marry a קטנה because she might turn out to be an אילונית (רבי מאיר's concern for the minority), and an אילונית is a זונה (רבי יהודה)

steps.title: Does רבי אליעזר really hold like רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the first half of רבה's explanation by bringing a ברייתא with רבי מאיר's ruling that minors do neither חליצה nor יבום, and the חכמים asking him why there is no יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי אליעזר really hold like רבי מאיר? A ברייתא teaches: a boy minor and a girl minor do not do חליצה and do not do יבום. That is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים said to him: you are right about חליצה, because the פסוק says 'man,' and we compare a woman to a man. But why no יבום?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts attacking רבה's explanation from step 5 by asking whether רבי אליעזר really agrees with רבי מאיר. It begins quoting a ברייתא as the setup for the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה needed רבי אליעזר to share רבי מאיר's worry that a young girl might turn out to be an אילונית. To test that, the גמרא first lays out where רבי מאיר's worry shows up: his ruling that minors cannot do יבום. The חכמים accept his ruling on חליצה, because it needs an adult, but they ask him why he also bans יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a source used to challenge)
The ceremony that releases a widow from marrying her late husband's brother
Marriage of a childless widow to her late husband's brother
We compare one case to another, so they share the same law

phrases.english: And does he hold like רבי מאיר?
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אליעזר. This questions רבה's explanation from step 5.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
A boy minor and a girl minor
do not do חליצה and do not do יבום,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.
They said to רבי מאיר:
You spoke well that they do not do חליצה.
"Man" is written in the section,
phrases.notes: דברים 25:7–10. A "man" means an adult, not a minor.

phrases.english: and we compare a woman to a man.
But what is the reason they do not do יבום?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מִי סָבַר לַהּ? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the first part of רבה's combined explanation from steps 5 and 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that רבי אליעזר holds like רבי מאיר and worries about the minority.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a source shows רבי אליעזר ignores the worry that a minor girl may be an אילונית, he cannot be relying on רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רבי מאיר explains: the minor might turn out unable to have children
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, רבי מאיר answers that a boy minor might turn out to be a סריס and a girl minor might turn out to be an אילונית, so the יבום could turn out to be a forbidden relationship.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: a boy minor might turn out to be a סריס, and a girl minor might turn out to be an אילונית. Then they would turn out to have been with an ערוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר answers the חכמים' question inside the ברייתא. This answer shows clearly that רבי מאיר worries a girl minor might be an אילונית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יבום is only allowed when it can carry on the brother's family. Otherwise the widow stays forbidden as a brother's wife. If the minor later turns out unable to have children, the יבום was never valid, and they would have been with a forbidden relative. This is the 'worry about the minority' that רבה relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who cannot father children
A woman who never develops and cannot have children
Being with a forbidden relative

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: Some versions have these words and some don't. Either way, רבי מאיר is the one answering.

phrases.english: A boy minor: in case he turns out to be a סריס,
a girl minor: in case she turns out to be an אילונית,
and they will turn out to have been with a forbidden relative.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: קָטָן שֶׁמָּא יִמָּצֵא סָרִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' question inside the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי מאיר forbids minors to do יבום.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the minor may turn out to be a סריס or an אילונית, which would make the relationship forbidden.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר allows a girl minor to do יבום
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא shows that רבי אליעזר allows a קטנה to do יבום, so he does not share רבי מאיר's worry about an אילונית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is taught: a girl minor may do יבום but does not do חליצה. That is רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the punch line of the challenge. רבי אליעזר lets a girl minor do יבום, which רבי מאיר forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר bans a minor girl's יבום only because she might be an אילונית. רבי אליעזר allows it, so he is clearly not worried about that. This seems to knock out the first half of רבה's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: She may do יבום
A girl minor

steps.whyThisMatters: רבה's explanation needed רבי אליעזר to worry that a minor might be an אילונית. This source suggests he does not.

phrases.english: And it is taught:
A girl minor may do יבום but does not do חליצה,
these are the words of רבי אליעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: קְטַנָּה מִתְיַיבֶּמֶת וְאֵינָהּ חוֹלֶצֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge by showing רבי אליעזר rules against רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר does not hold like רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי אליעזר allows a girl minor to do יבום.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that רבי אליעזר holds like רבי מאיר and worries that a minor girl may turn out to be an אילונית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר forbids a minor girl's יבום only because she might be an אילונית. רבי אליעזר allows it, so he does not share that worry.

steps.title: Does רבי אליעזר really hold like רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now questions the second half of רבה's explanation. It brings a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר defines a זונה simply as the name means, followed by רבי עקיבא's and רבי מתיא בן חרש's definitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי אליעזר really hold like רבי יהודה? A ברייתא teaches: a זונה is what the name means. That is רבי אליעזר's view. רבי עקיבא says a זונה is a woman who is available to anyone. רבי מתיא בן חרש says: even if her husband took her to drink the סוטה waters and was with her on the way, he made her a זונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second half of רבה's explanation. It quotes a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר gives his own definition of זונה, and it is not אילונית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה needed רבי אליעזר to agree with רבי יהודה that an אילונית is a זונה. But in this ברייתא, רבי אליעזר says a זונה is simply what the word means, a woman who acted immorally. The other opinions show the ברייתא is a list of different definitions.

keyTerms.meaning: A זונה is what the name says, a woman who acted immorally
A woman who is available to anyone
To make her drink the bitter waters of a סוטה

phrases.english: And does he hold like רבי יהודה?
But isn't it taught: "זונה" is a זונה as its name says,
these are the words of רבי אליעזר.
רבי עקיבא says: "זונה" is a woman available to anyone.
רבי מתיא בן חרש says:
Even if her husband went to make her drink,
phrases.notes: He means the bitter waters for a סוטה, a wife suspected of adultery.

phrases.english: and he was with her on the way,
he has made her a זונה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִי סָבַר לַהּ? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After challenging the רבי מאיר half, the גמרא now challenges the רבי יהודה half of רבה's explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that רבי אליעזר holds like רבי יהודה that an אילונית is a זונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר gives his own definition of זונה, an immoral woman. That leaves no room for counting an אילונית as a זונה.

steps.title: More definitions of זונה, including רבי יהודה's אילונית view
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי יהודה says a זונה is an אילונית. The חכמים say it is only a convert, a freed maidservant, or one who had an immoral relationship. רבי אלעזר says even an unmarried woman who was with a man outside marriage becomes a זונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: a זונה is an אילונית. The חכמים say: a זונה is only a convert, a freed maidservant, or a woman who had an immoral relationship. רבי אלעזר says: an unmarried man who is with an unmarried woman, not for marriage, has made her a זונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא. It shows that the 'אילונית is a זונה' view belongs to רבי יהודה, listed as a separate opinion from רבי אליעזר's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהודה and רבי אליעזר are listed as two different opinions in the same ברייתא, they clearly disagree. So רבי אליעזר does not seem to hold that an אילונית is a זונה. Both halves of רבה's explanation are now under challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A female convert
A freed maidservant
An unmarried man
For the purpose of marriage

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רבי אלעזר at the end with רבי אליעזר earlier. They are two different תנאים with two different views.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא has challenged both parts of רבה's explanation. רבי אליעזר allows a minor girl to do יבום, unlike רבי מאיר. He also defines זונה differently from רבי יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: זוֹנָה — זוֹ אַיְלוֹנִית.
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: a זונה is an אילונית.
And the חכמים say:
A זונה is only a female convert,
a freed maidservant, and a woman who had an immoral relationship.
רבי אלעזר says:
An unmarried man who is with an unmarried woman
not for the purpose of marriage,
has made her a זונה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: זוֹנָה זוֹ אַיְלוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, showing רבי יהודה's view is separate from רבי אליעזר's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה alone defines a זונה as an אילונית. The חכמים and רבי אלעזר give other definitions.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: it is about a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explains that רבי אליעזר is talking about a כהן גדול. A minor's marriage only fully takes hold once she grows up, and by then she is already a בעולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אדא בר אהבה said: here we are dealing with a כהן גדול. When does he truly acquire her? Only when she grows up. And when she grows up, she is already a בעולה.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבה's explanation was knocked down, the גמרא offers a brand-new reason for רבי אליעזר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול must marry a בתולה. If his marriage to a minor only becomes complete once she is grown, and they already lived together before that, then at the moment the marriage takes effect she is no longer a בתולה.

keyTerms.meaning: The High Priest, who must marry a בתולה
He acquires her (the marriage takes effect)
When she grows up
A woman who has already had relations (not a בתולה)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Here we are dealing with a High Priest.
When does he acquire her?
When she grows up.
[And when she grows up] she is already a non-virgin.
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording, repeating the phrase: only once she grows up, and by then she's already a בעולה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבה's explanation, which was challenged in steps 7 and 10, with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation of the case (limits it to a כהן גדול)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר's ban was based on the worry of an אילונית being a זונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban is about a כהן גדול, whose minor wife is no longer a בתולה by the time the marriage takes full effect.

steps.title: רבא rejects רב אדא בר אהבה's explanation
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the explanation makes no sense. If her father married her off, the marriage works right away. If she married herself off, everyone would agree, not only רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: this is without reason! If her father betrothed her, he acquires her from that very moment. And if she betrothed herself, is this only רבי אליעזר's view and not the רבנן's?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the explanation from step 12 by checking both possible ways the minor could have been married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a father marries off his minor daughter, the marriage is fully valid at once, so she is still a בתולה when it takes effect. If she married herself off as a minor, the problem would be so obvious that the חכמים would agree too, so it would not be a special opinion of רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Without reason (literally, 'without heart')
Her father betrothed her
She betrothed herself

phrases.english: Rava said: This is without reason.
If her father betrothed her,
he acquires her from that very moment.
And if she betrothed herself,

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא וְלָא רַבָּנַן?
phrases.english: is this the view of Rabbi Eliezer and not of the Rabbis?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מְכַלֵּי לֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges and rejects the explanation of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's explanation that the issue is a כהן גדול whose marriage takes effect only once she is grown.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible cases fail. A father's betrothal works immediately, and a self-betrothal would be a point everyone agrees on, not a special opinion of רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבא: any כהן, out of worry she will be seduced
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי אליעזר means even an ordinary כהן. We worry that the young wife might be seduced by another man while married to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: really it is about an ordinary כהן, and we are concerned that she might be seduced by another man while married to him.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the כהן גדול explanation, רבא gives his own reason for רבי אליעזר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A young, naive wife might be talked into a relationship with another man. That would make her forbidden to her כהן husband.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (going back to the plain reading)
An ordinary כהן (not the כהן גדול)
We are concerned
She will be seduced

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Actually it is about an ordinary priest,
and we are concerned lest she be seduced while married to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: לְעוֹלָם בְּכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting step 12, רבא offers a new explanation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban applies only to a כהן גדול because she would no longer be a בתולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban applies to every כהן, because a minor wife might be seduced and become forbidden to him.

steps.title: Then the same worry should apply to a ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the worry is seduction, why only a כהן? A ישראל's wife who is seduced is also forbidden to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a ישראל should also be forbidden to marry a minor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's reason by pointing out that it seems to apply to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife who willingly has a relationship with another man is forbidden even to a ישראל husband. So the worry about seduction should stop a ישראל from marrying a minor too, yet רבי אליעזר only spoke about a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
A regular Jew (not a כהן)

phrases.english: If so, an Israelite also should be forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי יִשְׂרָאֵל נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's explanation in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reason, the worry that the minor wife will be seduced.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That worry would forbid her to any husband, so it does not explain why רבי אליעזר limited the ruling to a כהן.

steps.title: Seducing a minor counts as אונס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that seducing a minor counts as אונס. A wife who suffered אונס stays permitted to a ישראל but not to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The seduction of a minor counts as rape, and a woman who was raped is fully permitted to a ישראל husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by explaining why the worry only matters for a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A minor is not considered able to truly agree, so even if she is persuaded, it counts as אונס. A wife who suffered אונס is still allowed to a ישראל husband, but a כהן's wife becomes forbidden to him even through אונס.

keyTerms.meaning: Seduction (she was persuaded)
A forced relationship (rape)
Is fully permitted

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, רבי אליעזר's worry is seduction. For a minor that counts as אונס, which only forbids a wife to a כהן.

phrases.english: The seduction of a minor is considered rape,
and a rape victim married to an Israelite is fully permitted to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: פִּתּוּיי קְטַנָּה אוֹנֶס הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 and saves רבא's explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Legal distinction between a כהן and a ישראל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Seduction would forbid the wife to any husband, so a ישראל should also be included.
steps.terutzMaskana: A minor's seduction counts as אונס, which forbids her only to a כהן, so only a כהן is told not to marry a minor.

steps.title: רב פפא: a כהן גדול, following a specific תנא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says רבי אליעזר's ruling is about a כהן גדול, and that it matches the view of a תנא in a ברייתא he is about to quote.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it is about a כהן גדול, and this follows the תנא of the following ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a third explanation and sets up a ברייתא to back it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רב אדא בר אהבה, רב פפא does not rely on the timing of the marriage. He bases the ban on a source that says a כהן גדול simply may not marry a minor at all.

keyTerms.meaning: This תנא (the teacher of the ברייתא about to be quoted)
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is about a High Priest,
and it follows this tanna, as it is taught:

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: בְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation from רבא's, going back to the כהן גדול idea of step 12 but on a new basis.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation tied to a ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban applies to every כהן because of the worry of seduction (רבא).
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban applies to a כהן גדול, following a תנא who says a כהן גדול may only marry a נערה.

steps.title: The ברייתא: a כהן גדול marries a נערה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads the words בתולה and אשה together. A כהן גדול must marry a girl who is past being a minor but not yet a בוגרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'בתולה'. You might think a minor is allowed, so the פסוק says 'אשה'. If 'אשה', you might think a בוגרת is allowed, so the פסוק says 'בתולה'. How so? She has left minority but has not yet reached full adulthood.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the ברייתא רב פפא quoted. It shows a source that does not let a כהן גדול marry a קטנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word of the פסוק rules out one end. 'אשה' rules out a minor, and 'בתולה' rules out a בוגרת. The only age left is a נערה, so according to this תנא a כהן גדול may not marry a קטנה, just as רבי אליעזר ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: A virgin
A woman (an adult, not a little girl)
A minor girl
A fully grown young woman, past the נערה stage
Minority, the stage of being a minor
Full adulthood

steps.whatToRemember: After רבה's explanation is challenged, the גמרא brings new explanations of רבי אליעזר: רב אדא בר אהבה (כהן גדול, timing of the marriage, rejected by רבא), רבא (any כהן, worry of seduction), רב פפא (a כהן גדול must marry a נערה), and, in the next steps, רב נחמן בר יצחק (also a כהן גדול, from a different ברייתא).
steps.confusionAlert: There are three age stages: קטנה (minor), נערה (the short stage right after), and בוגרת (fully grown). The ברייתא only allows the middle stage.

phrases.english: "A virgin": one might think even a minor;
therefore the verse says: "a woman."
If "a woman," one might think even a grown woman;
therefore the verse says: "a virgin."
How so?
She has left the category of minority,
but has not yet reached the category of full adulthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״בְּתוּלָה״, יָכוֹל קְטַנָּה — תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אִשָּׁה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the ברייתא that רב פפא said רבי אליעזר's ruling follows.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that רבי אליעזר's ban on marrying a minor is about a כהן גדול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'בתולה' and 'אשה' in the פסוק to require that a כהן גדול marry only a נערה.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives another way to explain רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says רבי אליעזר's ruling follows the view of a תנא in a ברייתא he is about to quote.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is the view of this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches:
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא offers another explanation of רבי אליעזר. He is setting up a ברייתא that he will quote in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another answer alongside רב פפא's answer from step 17. Like רב פפא, רב נחמן בר יצחק ties רבי אליעזר's ruling to a תנא's reading of the פסוק about a כהן גדול. His ברייתא, however, learns the rule from the word בתולה alone.

keyTerms.meaning: It is this תנא: the ruling matches this particular Tanna's view
As a ברייתא teaches
An אמורא who gives this explanation

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is the view of this tanna,
phrases.notes: He means that רבי אליעזר's ruling is about a כהן גדול and fits this תנא's view.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita:

steps.triggerLanguage: רב נחמן בר יצחק אמר האי תנא הוא דתניא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another answer alongside רב פפא's answer in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties the ruling to a specific תנא and to the case of a כהן גדול
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought רבי אליעזר's ruling was about any כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: His ruling is about a כהן גדול, following a תנא who reads בתולה as meaning a נערה.

steps.title: The ברייתא: בתולה means a נערה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that the word בתולה, used for the wife of a כהן גדול, means only a נערה. It brings a פסוק about רבקה as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן גדול must marry a "virgin." The word "virgin" means only a young woman (נערה). And so the פסוק says: "And the young woman was very beautiful, a virgin."
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק quotes the ברייתא. It shows from a פסוק that the word בתולה refers to a נערה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק about רבקה, the תורה calls her both נערה and בתולה, so the two words go together. A minor is not yet a נערה, so a כהן גדול may not marry her. That is exactly רבי אליעזר's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A virgin, the kind of woman a כהן גדול must marry
A young woman who is past being a minor (about age 12 to 12½)
And so the פסוק says: introduces a supporting פסוק

phrases.english: "A virgin" (the High Priest must marry),
and "virgin" means only a na'arah.
And so the verse says:
"And the maiden was very fair to look upon, a virgin."

steps.triggerLanguage: בתולה אין בתולה אלא נערה וכן הוא אומר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the ברייתא that step 19 promised.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that a כהן גדול may not marry a minor
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading בתולה as נערה, backed by בראשית 24:16

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: relations outside marriage make a woman a זונה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that when an unmarried man lives with an unmarried woman without the intent to marry her, she becomes a זונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: An unmarried man who has relations with an unmarried woman, not for the sake of marriage, has made her a זונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר's opinion from the ברייתא it discussed earlier. It is setting up a ruling on whether we follow him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, relations outside of marriage give the woman the status of זונה, even when both are single. A זונה is forbidden to marry a כהן, so his view is very strict.

keyTerms.meaning: An unmarried man / an unmarried woman
For the sake of marriage
A woman with a status that forbids her to marry a כהן

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
an unmarried man who has relations with an unmarried woman
not for the sake of marriage
has made her a zonah.
phrases.notes: That would make her forbidden to marry a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי אלעזר אומר פנוי הבא על הפנויה שלא לשם אישות עשאה זונה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to another opinion in the earlier ברייתא about who counts as a זונה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Single people living together outside of marriage make the woman a זונה.

steps.title: רב עמרם: the הלכה does not follow רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם rules that we do not follow רבי אלעזר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said: The הלכה is not like רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם gives the final ruling on רבי אלעזר's opinion: we do not follow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this ruling, an unmarried woman does not become a זונה just from relations outside of marriage. She therefore stays permitted to a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה does not follow this person
The אמורא who gives the ruling

steps.whatToRemember: We do not follow רבי אלעזר. An unmarried woman does not become a זונה just from relations outside of marriage.

phrases.english: Rav Amram said:
The halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב עמרם אין הלכה כרבי אלעזר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the opinion quoted in step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה does not follow רבי אלעזר's strict view on זונה.

steps.title: The משנה: when a man may stop trying to have children
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a man may not stop the מצוה of פריה ורביה until he has children. בית שמאי say two sons are needed, and בית הלל say a son and a daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man may not stop being fruitful and multiplying unless he has children. בית שמאי say: two sons. בית הלל say: a son and a daughter, as the פסוק says: "Male and female He created them."
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins on a new topic, the מצוה to have children. It explains how many children a man needs before he has done the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that a man must keep trying until he has children. They argue about which children fulfill the מצוה. בית הלל learn from the פסוק about creation that a son and a daughter are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין: our משנה
The מצוה to be fruitful and multiply, meaning to have children
He may not stop or neglect
The two great schools of Tannaim

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new משנה within the same פרק, not a new chapter.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A man may not stop from being fruitful and multiplying

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ לוֹ בָּנִים.
phrases.english: unless he has children.
Beit Shammai say: two males,
and Beit Hillel say: a male and a female,
as it is said: "Male and female He created them."

steps.triggerLanguage: לא יבטל אדם מפריה ורביה אלא אם כן יש לו בנים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man must keep trying to have children until he has them. בית שמאי require two sons, and בית הלל require a son and a daughter.

steps.title: The גמרא reads the משנה closely: he still needs a wife
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's wording, the גמרא learns that once a man has children he has finished פריה ורביה, but he may still not stop having a wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if he has children, he may stop from being fruitful and multiplying. But he may not stop from having a wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an inference from the exact words of the משנה. It is setting up a support for an אמורא's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says he may stop from פריה ורביה. It does not say he may stop being married. So the גמרא infers that the duty to have a wife continues even after he has children.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא: the discussion of the משנה begins
This implies: introduces an inference from the wording
He may stop or neglect

phrases.english: GEMARA:
This implies that if he has children,
he may stop from being fruitful and multiplying,
but from having a wife he may not stop.

steps.triggerLanguage: הא יש לו בנים מפריה ורביה בטיל מאשה לא בטיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes an inference from the wording of the משנה in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after having children, a man may not stop having a wife.

steps.title: This supports רב נחמן in the name of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The inference supports רב נחמן, who said in the name of שמואל that even a man with many children may not live without a wife, based on the פסוק "It is not good for man to be alone."
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports what רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: Even if a man has many children, he may not stay without a wife, as the פסוק says: "It is not good that the man should be alone."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that its reading of the משנה backs up a ruling of רב נחמן in the name of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's ruling has its own source, a פסוק about אדם being alone. Now the משנה's wording backs up the same idea. The duty to have children and the duty to have a wife are two separate duties.

keyTerms.meaning: This supports him
It is forbidden to stay without a wife
Alone

steps.whatToRemember: Having children completes פריה ורביה, but a man must still have a wife, because "it is not good for man to be alone."
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea that being married is its own obligation, separate from the מצוה of having children.

phrases.english: This supports Rav Nachman,
who said in the name of Shmuel.
For he said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ לְאָדָם כַּמָּה בָּנִים,
phrases.english: Even if a man has several children,
it is forbidden to remain without a wife,
as it is said: "It is not good that the man should be alone."

steps.triggerLanguage: מסייעא ליה לרב נחמן אמר שמואל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from step 24 to support an אמורא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling in the name of שמואל that a man may not live without a wife
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of the משנה, together with בראשית 2:18

steps.title: A second version: with children, he may stop having a wife
steps.stepSummary: Some say the inference from the משנה is that once a man has children, he may stop both פריה ורביה and having a wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: this means that if he has children, he may stop the מצוה of פריה ורביה, and he may also stop having a wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the inference from the משנה's words. In this version, once a man has children he may stop having a wife altogether.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24, the inference was that he finished פריה ורביה but must still have a wife. This version reads the משנה the opposite way: after having children, both obligations are gone. That sets up a direct clash with רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces a second version of the discussion
May stop, may set aside
The מצוה to be fruitful and multiply

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion arguing with step 24. It is a different version of the same inference, as some people received the discussion differently.

phrases.english: And some say:
This implies that if he has children,
he may stop from being fruitful and multiplying,
and he may also stop from having a wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an opposite reading of the משנה's implication from the one given in steps 24-25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once a man has children, he may stop פריה ורביה and also stop having a wife.

steps.title: Does this refute רב נחמן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether this version refutes רב נחמן in the name of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of what רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that this version of the inference seems to contradict רב נחמן in the name of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל that even a man with many children may not live without a wife (step 25). If the משנה implies he may stop having a wife, then רב נחמן's ruling would be disproven by a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say
A refutation: a strong challenge from a source that seems to disprove a view

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation
of רב נחמן who said in the name of שמואל!
phrases.notes: He ruled that even with many children, a man may not live without a wife (step 25).

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling using the second version of the inference.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן in the name of שמואל: a man may not live without a wife even if he has children.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה, read this way, implies that a man with children may stop having a wife, which contradicts רב נחמן.

steps.title: With children, he may marry a woman who cannot bear children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה only means a man with children may marry a woman who cannot have children, not that he may live without a wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. If he has no children, he must marry a woman who can have children. If he has children, he may marry a woman who cannot have children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the refutation. It explains what 'stop having a wife' really means in this version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Stop having a wife' does not mean living alone. It means he no longer needs a wife who can bear children. So he still needs a wife, and רב נחמן's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman able to have children
A woman not able to have children

phrases.english: No:
if he has no children,
he marries a woman capable of having children;
if he has children,
he may marry a woman who is not capable of having children.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא: אֵין לוֹ בָּנִים נוֹשֵׂא אִשָּׁה בַּת בָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing what 'stop having a wife' means.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A man with children may live without any wife at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: He still needs a wife; he just no longer needs one who can bear children.
steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, a man must always have a wife. Having children only frees him from needing a wife who can bear children.

steps.title: The practical difference: selling a ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: The practical difference is whether a man may sell a ספר תורה in order to marry for the sake of having children.
steps.simpleTranslation: The practical difference is selling a ספר תורה for the sake of children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the difference between having children and not having children matters in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man without children is still obligated in פריה ורביה, so he may sell a ספר תורה to marry a woman who can bear children. A man who already has children has fulfilled the מצוה, so he may not sell a ספר תורה for this.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical difference that results
A Torah scroll

phrases.english: The practical difference is
to sell a Torah scroll for the sake of children.
phrases.notes: He means selling it to pay for marrying a woman who can have children. That is allowed only for someone who has no children yet.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ לִמְכּוֹר סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה בִּשְׁבִיל בָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the practical result of the distinction made in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a man without children may sell a ספר תורה in order to marry and have children.
steps.whyThisMatters: Normally selling a ספר תורה is very restricted. This shows how high the מצוה of פריה ורביה ranks while it is still unfulfilled.

steps.title: What is בית שמאי's source for two males?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's words, 'two males,' and asks for בית שמאי's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: two males. What is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes בית שמאי's view. It asks where their view comes from, setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said בית שמאי require two sons. The גמרא now wants the source for that number.

keyTerms.meaning: Two males, meaning two sons
What is their reason?

phrases.english: בית שמאי say: two males.
What is the reason of בית שמאי?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמַיְיהוּ דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of having a wife and returns to the משנה's argument about how many children are needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for בית שמאי's requirement of two sons.

steps.title: בית שמאי learn from משה's two sons
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי learn from משה, who had two sons, גרשום and אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn it from משה, as it is written: 'The sons of משה: גרשום and אליעזר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בית שמאי learn from משה רבינו. He had two sons, so two sons must be enough to fulfill the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists only two children for משה, both sons. Since משה surely kept this מצוה, two sons must be enough to fulfill פריה ורביה.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn, we derive
The two sons of משה

phrases.english: We learn it from Moshe,
as it is written: “The sons of Moshe:
Gershom and Eliezer.”

steps.triggerLanguage: יָלְפִינַן מִמֹּשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי derive two sons from משה, who had only גרשום and אליעזר.

steps.title: בית הלל learn from the creation of the world
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל learn from the creation of the world, when people were created male and female.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל: we learn from the creation of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית הלל's source. They learn from how the world was created.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At creation, man was made male and female. So, according to בית הלל, a son and a daughter fulfill the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: The creation of the world

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel:
we learn from the creation of the world.
phrases.notes: Mankind was created male and female, so one son and one daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל: יָלְפִינַן מִבְּרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the matching source for the other side of the משנה's argument.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית הלל derive a son and a daughter from the creation of man as male and female.

steps.title: Why don't בית שמאי also learn from creation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why בית שמאי do not learn from the creation of the world like בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי, let them learn from the creation of the world!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בית שמאי. Creation seems like a strong source, so why not use it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Creation is the first and most basic model of having children. The גמרא wonders why בית שמאי would prefer the example of משה over it.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them learn

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai,
let them learn from the creation of the world!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי לֵילְפֵי מִבְּרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions בית שמאי's choice of source in light of בית הלל's source.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's use of משה as the source.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Creation is an available and basic source; בית שמאי should learn from it as בית הלל do.

steps.title: We do not learn what is possible from what was impossible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer for בית שמאי: we do not derive a case that is possible from one that was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not derive a case that is possible...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer for בית שמאי. The sentence continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that we do not learn a case where something is possible from a case where it was not possible. At creation there was only one way to create people, as one male and one female, so it is not a model for ordinary families.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not derive or compare
Possible

steps.confusionAlert: The answer is cut off at the end of this amud. The rest of the sentence continues on the next amud and finishes the comparison.

phrases.english: We do not derive a case that is possible
phrases.notes: The sentence finishes on the next amud: we don't learn a case where there's a choice from one where there was no other choice.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין דָּנִין אֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the source as not comparable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Creation should be the model for בית שמאי too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Creation was a case without other options, so it cannot teach about ordinary cases where there are choices.
